blocks.orig: The tropical island of Zanzibar is known for its beautiful white sandy beaches and coral reefs. But Zanzibar does not only offer laid-back beach life and watersports activities but also a colorful culture and history. The old Stone Town is an amazing mix of cultures. Food lovers and culture enthusiasts can visit interesting cultural places like Sultan’s Palace, the House of Wonders and Darajani or Forodhani food markets. You can go on a Spice Tour or explore the amazing coral reefs and swim among tropical reef fish. The opportunities are endless. We selected for you 4 great excursions to do when visiting Zanzibar.
blocks.html: Zanzibar, a tropical island, is famous for its stunning white beaches and coral reefs. Yet there is more to it than relaxed days on the sand and watersports: the island also has a rich, colourful history and culture. Old Stone Town is a remarkable blend of influences. If you enjoy food and culture, places such as the Sultan's Palace, the House of Wonders and the Darajani or Forodhani food markets are well worth a visit. Alternatively, join a Spice Tour or head out to the wonderful coral reefs to swim among tropical reef fish. There is no shortage of options. Here are 4 excellent excursions we picked out for your time on Zanzibar.

blocks.orig: Nakupenda Beach is a large sandbank in the middle of the ocean. This untouched ‘island’ is only 20 minutes away from Stone Town. Take a boat trip to the beautiful white sand beach with crystal clear water and tropical views. A great place to relax, sunbathe, swim, snorkel and enjoy the underwater world. If you are lucky, you can even see dolphins. A lot of operators also offer a delicious seafood lunch on the beach.
blocks.html: Nakupenda Beach is a big sandbank out in the open sea. This pristine 'island' lies just 20 minutes from Stone Town. A boat takes you to its gleaming white sand, crystal-clear water and tropical scenery, and once there you can relax, sunbathe, swim, snorkel and explore life beneath the surface. With a bit of luck you may spot dolphins too. Many operators include a tasty seafood lunch served right on the beach.

blocks.orig: Cheetah’s Rock is a unique rescue centre for wild animals. Here you can learn and interact with wildlife in a natural setting. The lady who runs the centre has a tremendous passion for wildlife and dedicated her life to protect these wild animals. All animals are well taken care of, live in large spaces where they are able to exercise and are not sedated by tranquillizers. If you love animals and like to have an up-close and personal encounter with a cheetah, lion, hyena, bush baby or dikdik, this is the place to visit. Although a visit is pricey, the tour is well worth it.
blocks.html: Cheetah's Rock is a one-of-a-kind rescue centre for wild animals, where you can learn about and interact with wildlife in natural surroundings. The woman who runs it has a deep passion for wildlife and has devoted her life to protecting these animals. All of them are well looked after, live in spacious enclosures with plenty of room to move, and are never sedated with tranquillisers. If you are an animal lover hoping for a close, personal encounter with a cheetah, lion, hyena, bush baby or dikdik, this is the place to go. The visit is not cheap, but the tour is worth every penny.

blocks.orig: Zanzibar is a true paradise for divers and snorkelers and the perfect spot for humpback whale watching. The migrating whales arrive in the waters around Zanzibar in late July and you can see them till November in this area. Humpback whales are easily distinguished from any other whale by their nodules and long flippers. These giants can be up to 55 metres in length. If you plan to go to Zanzibar during this time of the year, we definitely recommend you to go on a whale watching trip. If you are lucky, you can even spot them while you are swimming or scuba diving.
blocks.html: For divers and snorkellers Zanzibar is a genuine paradise, and it is also an ideal place to watch humpback whales. The whales arrive on their migration in the waters off Zanzibar in late July and stay in the area until November. You can tell a humpback apart from any other whale by its nodules and long flippers, and these giants can measure up to 55 metres. If your visit to Zanzibar falls in this period, we strongly recommend a whale watching trip. With luck, you may even see them while swimming or scuba diving.

blocks.orig: Sea turtles also nest around Zanzibar and are often see by divers, as well as several species of dolphins. The fortunate scuba divers may even spot a whale shark or manta ray.
blocks.html: The waters around Zanzibar are also a nesting ground for sea turtles, which divers frequently encounter, as they do several dolphin species. With a bit of luck a scuba diver might even come face to face with a whale shark or manta ray.

blocks.orig: Discover the mangrove forests on a paddleboard

Explore the mangrove forest by SUP (Stand Up Paddleboard). If you love nature, water and exciting adventures, this excursion may be something for you. Mangrove forests only grow in tropical areas near the equator and coastlines. It is a special sighting to see those dense knots of roots, appearing to be trees floating above the water. The mangroves are also a great place to spot all kind of birds and fish.
blocks.html: Take a SUP (Stand Up Paddleboard) through the mangrove forest. If you are drawn to nature, water and a bit of adventure, this trip could be just right for you. Mangroves grow only in tropical regions close to the equator and along coastlines, and the sight of their dense tangles of roots, like trees hovering above the water, is something special. The mangroves also attract a wide variety of birds and fish for you to spot.

blocks.orig: Feed the giant tortoise at Prison Island
blocks.html: Feed the giant tortoises on Prison Island

blocks.orig:
Prison Island is a deserted island that lies about half-hour by boat from Zanzibar Island. It
was once used as a place where slaves were detained. Later it became a quarantine station for people with deadly diseases. Nowadays, a lot of people go to Prison Island to relax and enjoy the peacefulness and lovely white beach. It is ideal for snorkeling, swimming or sunbathing. You can see the old prison ruins and about a hundred giant land tortoises that were imported from Seychelles in the 19th century. These turtles are one of the largest in the world and are walking free in the natural reserve where you can feed them.
blocks.html:
Prison Island is an uninhabited islet roughly half an hour by boat from Zanzibar Island. In
earlier times enslaved people were held here, and afterwards it became a quarantine post for patients with deadly illnesses. Today most visitors come simply to unwind, drawn by the tranquillity and the lovely white beach, which lends itself to snorkelling, swimming or sunbathing. You can wander through the ruins of the former prison and meet around a hundred giant land tortoises, brought over from the Seychelles in the 19th century. Few tortoises anywhere grow bigger, and they wander freely in the nature reserve, where you are welcome to feed them.
